title: What is the value of this string of tokens?
description: A string of one hundred tokens repeats three green tokens and then two red tokens. Zero pairs are cancelled in one block of five, and the value of one block is multiplied by the number of blocks. The video breaks the slip of thinking that the value of a string is just the number of its tokens.
teaching_notes: One idea: cancel the zero pairs in one repeating block, then count the blocks. Watch for students who give the number of tokens as the value, forgetting that a red token is worth minus one.

video_script.why: The child finds the value of a long string of green and red tokens by cancelling zero pairs in one repeating block and counting the blocks.
video_script.substitution: The book's string of 100 tokens, green tokens worth +1 and red tokens worth −1, read in blocks of three green then two red.
video_script.anchor: the string of green and red tokens of the book, drawn along the whole stage
video_script.payoff_line: The value of the string is twenty

final_answer.spoken: the value of the string is twenty

never_show: the claim that the value equals the number of tokens
maths_rules: in one block, 2 zero pairs cancel, so (+3) + (−2) = +1
check: 20 blocks give 60 green and 40 red; 40 zero pairs cancel; (+60) + (−40) = +20
video_script.design: The long string sits across the stage with its repeating block of five tokens bracketed. One block is shown cancelling to a single green token, then the blocks are counted.
open_questions: The picture of the string is not in the extracted book text; the pattern of 3 green then 2 red comes from the worklist steps and the old migration note (60 green, 40 red).
